messages.subject: Re: CODEX qc
parts:
Hi Lennart,

Thanks for your interest in CODEX! CODEX does apply a very simple and straightforward qc procedure on samples:

sampfilter <- apply(Y, 2, sum) > 2000
Y_qc <- Y[, sampfilter]
sampname_qc <- sampname[sampfilter]

Basically it’s to capture the ‘bad’ samples that fail to be captured, which we do see from our whole-exome sequencing pipeline as well as the targeted sequencing pipeline, although they are fairly rare. For the samples that show a great amount of post-segmentation CNV calls, I would suggest either drop them and redo the analysis as they may interfere with the normalization procedure. Another option is to apply a threshold on the CNVs identified (e.g., number of exons within or length of the CNV discovered).

Hope this clarifies! Also, I am copying our mailing list so that people have similar questions as yours will see this post.

Cheers,
Yuchao


On Jan 6, 2016, at 9:47 AM, Johansson, LF <l.joh...@umcg.nl> wrote:

Dear Dr. Jiang,
 
My name is Lennart Johansson and I am a bioinformatician at the department of Genetics of the University Medical Center Groningen in the Netherlands.
I succesfully ran CODEX on a series of samples, and now I am looking through the results. The qcmat.txt files show the qc metrics of all targets, are there also such metrics for the samples?
For some samples I get lots of calls and I suspect that probably I should disregard results for those samples.
 
Thank you in advance for your answer.

Best regards,
 
Lennart Johansson
l.joh...@umcg.nl
